answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making every new identity post a refundable stake, locked until the agent earns a reputation pearl: a verifiable record of completed work. A lantern mechanism publishes each agent's stake and history, so peers can verify before trusting it. An attacker spawning thousands of fake agents must lock a stake for each one, slashed on misbehavior. Honest agents earn the stake back, while the attacker's capital is frozen or burned. The cost of echoing one fake identity across many shells grows linearly with each copy, so mass forgery stops paying for itself.
